t: Syndicalists held that unions, not political parties, should wage the class struggle by direct action and the general strike, and that union federations would manage production and replace the state after a revolution.

Syndicalist organisations such as the CGT in France, the CNT in Spain, the USI in Italy, the FAUD in Germany and the FORA in Argentina reached their height between about 1910 and the early 1920s, and in Spain from 1936 put much of the economy under workers' control until the Nationalist victory.

Scholars disagree on the word itself: some apply it to every revolutionary, direct-action union movement, including the IWW, while others, such as Larry Peterson, use five criteria that exclude the IWW and the Canadian One Big Union.
dyk: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, a root of syndicalist thought, coined the word capitalist, and Émile Pouget said that the idea of the general strike came to France from the United States, fertilised by the blood of the anarchists hanged in Chicago.
ev: The French General Confederation of Labour (CGT) is formed; it advocates the general strike from the start
The Industrial Workers of the World is founded in the United States
The CGT adopts the Charter of Amiens, reaffirming its independence from party politics
The Italian syndicalist confederation USI is formed by veterans of the farm and factory strikes
The First International Syndicalist Congress meets in London but does not found an international
The Free Workers' Union of Germany (FAUD) is formed in December
The International Workers' Association is formed as an international syndicalist federation
The Spanish Revolution puts much of Spain's economy under workers' control, with the CNT as the main union organisation of the Republican side

f.thinkers: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, whose mutualism was its direct root; Mikhail Bakunin, who advocated the general strike; Émile Pouget, anarchist and CGT leader who backed sabotage and direct action; Victor Griffuelhes of the CGT; Bill Haywood and Vincent St. John of the IWW; James Larkin of the Irish ITGWU; Tom Mann of Britain; Rudolf Rocker, who wrote the FAUD's programme; Georges Sorel, whose Reflections on Violence brought syndicalist ideas to a wider audience
f.texts: The Charter of Amiens (adopted by the CGT in 1906); Georges Sorel, Reflections on Violence (English edition 1912); Ford and Foster, Syndicalism (1913); the Industrial Workers of the World, The IWW: What it is and what it is not (1928); Rudolf Rocker, Anarcho-syndicalism: Theory and Practice (1938)
f.ideas: irreconcilable class struggle between workers and the bourgeoisie; unions as both organs of struggle within capitalism and the embryo of a new society; direct action, sabotage and above all the general strike; independence of unions from political parties; federalism over centralism; replacement of the state by workers' organisations; production managed by the workers
f.today: The International Workers' Association (IWA–AIT) exists with very little influence; the Spanish CNT had around 50,000 members in 2018 and the CGT, which split from it, around 100,000; the German FAU, the British Solidarity Federation and Sweden's SAC Syndikalisterna carry on the tradition; the International Confederation of Labour was formed in 2018
